category_title: Dominant preschool children who frequently report peers' norm violations
scenario_title: Resource dispute and property entitlement during free play
minimal_context: Jack is participating in free play at the art and block stations with his peers.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Jack, you and Matthew can use the building blocks to make a tower, or use the scissors and paintbrushes at the art table.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Teacher, I want to paint but she’s not ﬁnished yet [with the paintbrush]; she won’t hurry up.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just see if you can find something else to do while you wait.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Walks over to the blocks) Give me those blocks, Matthew. If you don't give them to me, I’m telling the teacher!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Try to play nicely and work it out together.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Teacher! Matthew, he’s knocking down the tower! And he won’t let me have the scissors! You need to punish him!

task.content: Engaging in free play and daily classroom activities

context.materials: Scissors, paintbrushes, and building blocks for a tower
context.social_setting: Interacting with peers during free play

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When another child does not share a resource, damages property, or engages in a perceived aggressive action
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Uses the threat of tattling as a strategic sanction against a peer's unwelcome behavior and directly reports the transgression to the teacher
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Highly egocentric, focused on achieving help or punishment for another child's negative behavior toward the tattler
related_quotes: He won’t let me have the scissors
Matthew, he’s knocking down the tower
She’s not ﬁnished yet [with the paintbrush]; she won’t hurry up

behavior_patterns.condition: When experiencing retaliatory impulses against peers' aggression in an environment where physical aggression is punished
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Directs impulses into indirect, verbal behavior by reporting the peer's actions to the teacher
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Using tattling as an interpersonal strategy to achieve social dominance and manipulate others' attention
